The problem

Context

R&E Tours is owned and operated by Rick Klimek. Rick initially needed IT support for his business, which eventually expanded to hosting, domain management, and website design.

Rick wanted the digital side of his business consolidated. There were three domain registrars, two hosting companies, and two email providers, with fees that kept increasing year after year. This meant rebuilding his primary website, r-etours.com.

Constraints

The old site ran on a proprietary website builder that couldn’t be moved to another host, so it had to be rebuilt from scratch. Rick also had a firm requirement: the new site had to look identical to the old one.

Key decisions

Rebuilding the builder’s components

The old site was made from the platform’s pre-built pieces, like the theme, stylized components like banners, the photo gallery, contact forms, and navigation. I had to rebuild each one from scratch so it looked and behaved the same, with no access to the original code.

Options I weighed

  • [Option A — why not]
  • [Option B — why not]
  • [Option C — chosen, and the evidence behind it]

Switching over with little to no downtime

Rick needed to minimize disruption for teachers and advisors, so I built and tested the new site on a staging server and switched the domain over in one planned cutover.

Adding what the old site couldn’t do

Rick wanted to accept online payments for trip deposits and a way to update tour dates and prices himself without calling me. These had to fit the existing look so nobody could tell they were new.
